jessica (support): Heads-up — enterprise customer (Acme) hit a hard error from embeddings endpoint. They say a sudden spike in 400s and "dimension mismatch" on a subset of requests :grimacing:

sam (ingest): Can you paste the request body they used? single vs batch mixups are common here.

jessica (support): Yep. Replicating snippet from their agent: 
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "text-embed-003",
  "input": [["Quarterly report summary"]],
  "user_id": "acct-ACME-123"
}
```
They claim the returned embedding has length 1534 but their downstream expects 1536. Some requests succeed, others fail.

sam (ingest): Looks like double-wrapped input (nested array). SDKs sometimes wrap singletons in an extra array for batch-if-needed. Our runtime treats the outer array as batch -> OK, but inner array becomes tokenized differently? :thinking:

mike (sre): Also check if some requests were gzipped/ndjson or had Content-Type issues. If the client sometimes sends a stringified JSON instead of raw JSON it can turn arrays into strings on our side and break shape parsing.

jessica (support): Customer says they use a custom wrapper that conditionally JSON.stringify the body when retrying. Example of failing header: `Content-Type: application/json` but payload ends up `\"[...[\"]\"` (string).

carlos (pm): Can we reproduce quickly with curl? If we can reproduce, give them repro steps and a minimal fix (flatten input).

sam (ingest): Repro attempt on my laptop:
```bash
# failing (double-wrapped)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"text-embed-003","input":[["hello world"]]}'

# succeeds (flatten)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"text-embed-003","input":["hello world"]}'
```
When the inner array is present the server returns 400: `embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1534` in some cases (depends on tokenizer path).

jessica (support): Pasting exact error body from their logs: `{"error":"invalid_embedding_shape","message":"expected vector length 1536 for model text-embed-003, got 1534"}`

mike (sre): Filed quick checklist: 1) confirm content-type and body not JSON-stringified 2) check client's retry wrapper for double-serialization 3) run a small batch test at scale to ensure no batching-induced trimming of tokens 4) add logging for incoming Content-Length vs decoded JSON shape.

sam (ingest): I dug into our parser — if we receive a string for `input` we attempt to parse but only handle a single stringified list, not nested ones, which can lead to trimmed Unicode characters or escaping dropping 2 tokens -> 1534. I'll open a PR to harden parse and add a validation error that tells the client to flatten nested arrays.

carlos (pm): For immediate customer unblock, give them a 1-liner fix and a short repro so they can patch client: "Ensure `input` is an array of strings (or an array of arrays for batch), but don't wrap a singleton again. Example: \"input\": [\"text\"] not \"input\": [[\"text\"]]". Also ask for any proxy/retry middleware that might stringify bodies.

jessica (support): Sent them: short repro + workaround + request to share raw HTTP capture (curl or HAR).

redwood-support-bot: Ticket #S-4782 created and linked to customer account acct-ACME-123. SLA: response within 4h.

mike (sre): Quick mitigation: I'll add a temporary diagnostic flag that logs if `input` parses as nested-array-of-string-within-array and return a helpful 400 that calls out "remove inner array". Low-risk config change.

sam (ingest): PR #3284 opened to improve parser and error message. I'll add unit tests for stringified payloads and nested lists.

jessica (support): Customer confirmed they patched their retry wrapper to avoid JSON.stringify in retries and reported success on a small sample. Will confirm full rollout tomorrow. :relieved:

carlos (pm): Nice. Let's keep this in the backlog for a more explicit SDK FAQ and improve docs with an example for singletons vs batches.

jessica (support): Closing loop — will follow up when customer fully validated. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
